LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.headline: Seahawks rookie report: More misses than hits after week 6
away.blurb: ​It might be too far-fetched to say that the Seahawks and the 12 should be feeling good about guard Beau Stephens, but he is the only rookie consistently seeing the field. Stephens took 30 offensive snaps for the Seahawks against the Broncos. He continues to split the first-string right guard spot along with Christian Haynes while Anthony Bradford remains out with knee and hip injuries . ​The Seahawks’ coaching staff likes that Stephens is getting meaningful reps. The problem is that he is still struggling to find some consistency against NFL-caliber talent. Stephens has an overall grade of 4 8 by Pro Football Focus , which ranks 69th out of 75 eligible guards. There is a good chance that Bradford could return for the Seahawks for Week 7 at home versus the Kansas City Chiefs. This would likely cut Stephens’ reps to non-existent unless he plays on special teams, where he has only played a handful each game. It is still early to decide if the Seattle Seahawks' 2026 NFL Draft is a miss, but injuries and inconsistent play says otherwise. It doesn't help that the Seahawks encountered a Super Bowl hangover and there are signs that players and coaches are measuring up to their season expectations. The 2026 Draft class had mild expectations to contribute, but even those mild expectations aren't being met. ​The Seahawks are now 3-3 and coming off a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football. Only one rookie from the 2026 NFL Draft class participated in the game and they took reps more than normally would. There is still hope for this class to get better, but it is showing flashes of the 2013 or 2019 draft classes. ​The Seahawks added former undrafted running back Robert Henry Jr. from the Washington Commanders’ practice squad on Oct. 6. It was likely too soon to play him in the Week 5 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but there was a great opportunity for him to play in the game versus the Broncos. Instead, the Seahawks barely utilized the running game and had quarterback Sam Darnold drop back 56 times. Henry remains on the 53-man roster. ​Another undrafted rookie they acquired much later after the Draft, cornerback Avery Smith didn’t play in the game against the Broncos. He played 16 special teams snaps against the 49ers, where he accounted for three total tackles. When Irv Smith Jr. got off IR , he took Smith’s place on special teams coverage. ​Not much changes from the rookies that remain on the practice squad roster. There aren’t any moves from the nine rookies on the practice squad due to the short week in between the 49ers and the Broncos. ​Seattle’s first-round running back Jadarian Price missed his third consecutive game while he is on IR with a chest injury. He will miss the Week 7 home game versus the Kansas City Chiefs. But Charbonnet isn't the only Seahawks running back approaching a return. Rookie Jadarian Price is also making progress from his injury, giving Seattle hope that its depleted backfield could soon look considerably different. When Will Zach Charbonnet Return to Seahawks? The fourth-year running back has been practicing since October 1, when the Seahawks opened his 21-day return window. Under NFL rules, Seattle must activate him to the 53-man roster before that window expires or leave him on PUP for the remainder of the season. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler also reported on October 14 that Charbonnet had a "legitimate chance" to return against Kansas City, citing multiple sources. However, Charbonnet was ruled out of Seattle's October 15 loss to the Denver Broncos, leaving the team to rely on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani in the backfield. When Will Jadarian Price Return From Injury? While Charbonnet could return against Kansas City, rookie Jadarian Price will have to wait at least another week. Price remains on injured reserve with a chest injury and is not eligible to return for Seattle's October 25 matchup. His earliest possible return comes November 2 against the Chicago Bears . "He's doing great," Macdonald said. "We should be looking at a sooner-rather-than-later return after this game." Charbonnet rushed for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns during the 2025 regular season, giving the Seahawks an established option if he can return to full strength. Price offers a different dimension with his speed and explosiveness, although his return remains at least one game away. away.headline: Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising
away.blurb: Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Seahawks injury update: Jadarian Price return timeline sounds promising The Seattle Seahawks need running back help in the worst way. It'll be at least two weeks until Jadarian Price is eligible to return from injured reserve, while Zach Charbonnet has a chance to play against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7. Mike Macdonald revealed a little bit of a timeline as far as Price's return during his Friday morning show with Brock and Salk on Seattle Sports 710 . "He's doing great," Macdonald said. "We should be looking at a sooner rather than later return after this [Kansas City Chiefs] game." Price has been out since the start of Week 4 with a chest injury, which he aggravated in practice after getting the initial injury in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. The rookie out of Notre Dame has had a couple of costly fumbles , but since George Holani and Emanuel Wilson have also since lost a combined three fumbles, he's hardly the only culprit. Price has offered some explosiveness in the run game in a limited sample size, and his speed is what the main running back room lacks. Mookie Alexander Sat, October 17, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Mike Macdonald had no update on Charbonnet's progress (or, maybe, no update he was willing to share), but it's worth noting that Charbonnet must be activated this upcoming week or else he reverts to injured reserve for the rest of the season. Seattle opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 1, prior to the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Once that window expires, the Seahawks either have to place him on the 53-man roster or end his season. The latter is obviously not happening unless there's some unbelievably worrying setback, so we're left to turn our attention to Price. In an ideal world, Charbonnet is back in Week 7 and Price is back in Week 8, at which point the running back room should be a lot stronger.

The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. As Jaguars head coach Liam Coen noted this week, divisional games offer a chance for a different slate of circumstances compared to typical weeks. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. That's what's great about football, that's what's great about rivalries, is that you have a level of respect for each other," Coen said. "Because you know any given Sunday, anything can happen, especially in rivalry-type games and understanding what you can learn from each of these opportunities that you play against one another in, and how well you start to get to know each other in ways in terms of what they want to do, what we want to do. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps. But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season. So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan. Predicted Stat Line: 30% snap share, 4 TAR, 3 REC, 43 YDS, 1 TD DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps . "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do." So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks. Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position. A 30% snap share would likely be around the 15 to 20-snap mark. But in those limited looks, it feels likely that the Texans will involve him on a fair share of those plays––in this case, perhaps for four targets––to build up his confidence and rediscover some chemistry with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud . And in a best-case scenario for the Texans, maybe Harrison Jr. is able to haul in his second touchdown of the season so far. If Houston is within striking distance for a score, and there's an ideal situation for Harrison Jr. to fill into, why not start off the tenure with his new team on a good note? So in all, a 3-43-1 stat line feels like a modest projection for Harrison Jr. in game one. away.blurb: Ryans was hopeful about getting Dell on the field during the preseason. Dell participated on a limited basis during training camp, but landed on injured reserve to start the season. Houston Texans Announce Major Tank Dell News for New York Giants Game Unlock the latest Heavy on Texans news — direct to your inbox. The wait is over for Houston Texans wide receiver Tank Dell . "#Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said WR Tank Dell will be activated this week prior to the Giants game on Sunday," SportsTalk 790's Adam Wexler reported on X on October 19. Coach DeMeco Ryans lets reporters know WR Tank Dell will be back against the New York Giants The announcement drew national attention , with Dell set to play in a game for the first time since Week 16 of the 2024 season against the Kansas City Chiefs . He suffered a significant leg injury in that contest, resulting in multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap. Texans Get Tank Dell Back After Severe Leg Injury That meant he had to miss the first four games of the, season, which was already a setback from the preseason hopes. It has taken two additional weeks for the Texans to feel comfortable making Dell active for a game. His last game will have been 658 days ago come kickoff in Week 7. The Texans are taking on the New York Giants , who are 3-2-1 on the season and lead the NFC East, but could also be playing their third quarterback of the season in J.J. McCarthy . Dell, who turns 26 on October 29, was a third-round pick, taken with the 69th overall pick in the draft. He has 98 receptions for 1,376 yards and 10 touchdowns so far in his career, serving as one of quarterback C.J. Stroud's top targets. The Texans wide receiver room has been in flux this season. They lost would-be WR2 Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL a joint practice in training camp. WR1 and two-time Pro Bowler Nico Collins has missed time due to injuries, too. The Texans acquired Kayshon Boutte and Marvin Harrison Jr. in trades with the New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals, respectively, while Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel have taken meaningful steps in the offense this season. That all begs the question of how Dell fits with the current group. Nevertheless, the Texans are undoubtedly welcoming Dell back with open arms as they look to continue turning their season around coming off back-to-back wins. home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. away.headline: Chicago Bears defeat Atlanta Falcons 31-23 as quarterback Caleb Williams returns from injury
away.blurb: Bears fans celebrate Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday night matchup ATLANTA -- Caleb Williams completed his first 12 passes in his return from a hamstring injury, D'Andre Swift ran for two touchdowns and the Chicago Bears beat the Atlanta Falcons 31-23 on Sunday. Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon, who was activated from the physically unable to perform list before the game in his return from a calf injury, had three sacks and two forced fumbles. Gordon's big day was capped by a sack of Michael Penix Jr. and forced fumble with 2:54 remaining and the Bears protecting a 31-23 lead. The fumble was recovered by Devin Bush at the Atlanta 28. The Bears ran out the clock inside the Atlanta 5. After missing three games, Williams was both mobile and accurate in his impressive return for the Bears (4-2). He opened the game by completing 6 of 6 passes for 64 yards, including a 14-yard scoring pass to Colston Loveland, on Chicago's opening drive. Williams was 12 of 12 for 142 yards before throwing his first incompletion in the second quarter. Though the Bears won two of three games with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum filing in at quarterback, Williams' return sparked the offense. He completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards with one touchdown. Penix threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Jahan Dotson in the second quarter. The perfectly placed back-shoulder fade pass cut the Bears' lead to 14-7, but a fumbled fair catch attempt by Zachariah Branch gave Chicago possession at the Atlanta 10 late in the first half. Branch also lost a fumble on a kickoff return late in the third quarter. Bears fans celebrate win, Williams' return, look ahead to Thursday "Caleb balled out," Hasler said. "Bears played great and yeah bears are back in town ready for Thursday." Fans are already looking ahead to Thursday's game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field, anticipating another lively atmosphere as the Bears return home. Bears: DB Cam Lewis was evaluated for a concussion in the second quarter. RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) was inactive. RG Jonah Jackson was ruled doubtful to return with a hip injury in the third quarter. Falcons: ILB Kendal Daniels was carted off the field midway through the third quarter after making a helmet-first tackle on tight end Colston Loveland. Daniels' head snapped back and Falcons players circled Daniels as he was strapped onto the stretcher and driven off the field. He was officially ruled out with a neck injury and the Falcons announced he was alert and had movement in all extremities and was being evaluated at Grady Hospital in Atlanta . ... ILB Divine Deablo (arm) was ruled out in the second quarter. CB Avieon Terrell (left shoulder) left the game in the second quarter. DB Billy Bowman Jr. was ruled doubtful with a hamstring injury. away.headline: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Oct 17 (Field Level Media) - Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3).

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source. pic.twitter.com/O82hES7z4t After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved to 4.5 and now all the way to 5.5 following Adam Schefter's report. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites, a full one-point change from where the spread was on Tuesday morning . Still, Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday, which makes his status for Sunday a little murky. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that the two-time league MVP is "day-to-day." Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. While it would have been a positive sign for the Ravens for Jackson to practice on Wednesday, he still has time to log a session on Thursday or Friday before the team's matchup against Cleveland. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers about Jackosn's status and how it could impact this game. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Tyler Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out which is very helpful." On Wednesday, Fanatics Sportsbook explained to Sports Illustrated that they actually dropped their line from 5.5 to Ravens -5 after Jackson missed practice. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” The market seems to be putting a lot of stock into Schefter's report, but that could change quickly if the star quarterback logs another DNP on Thursday. Bettors may want to take a "wait-and-see" approach before committing to a bet on the Ravens, especially as more than field goal favorites. The Baltimore Ravens are no strangers to playing without their star quarterback, and that helps to explain why they're 3-point favorites on Sunday despite backup Tyler Huntley starting. My Ravens vs. Browns predictions back Baltimore to grind out a win while leaning on Derrick Henry, who can exploit a vulnerable Cleveland run defense. Here are my NFL picks ahead of this Sunday, Oct. 18, clash, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET today. Ravens vs Browns prediction today: Ravens -3.5 The Baltimore Ravens are chasing their fourth straight win over the Cleveland Browns , and Lamar Jackson's absence isn't deterring me from fading a Cleveland team that crashed back to earth last weekend. Even with Todd Monken's knowledge of his former team, I'll lay the points - playable anywhere from -3 to -4. Tyler Huntley , one of the NFL's better backup QBs, led Baltimore to an overtime win in Week 5, and he's now 3-0 as a starter since last season. But this pick is more about what Derrick Henry can do against a Browns defense that's allowing 117.4 rushing yards per game and could be without Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham (both questionable). On the other side of the ball, look for the visitors to be opportunistic against Deshaun Watson , who was sacked eight times in Week 5 and may have to do more in the passing game given the hosts' backfield injuries. The Ravens are 4-2 ATS in their past six road games , and two of the last three meetings between these teams have been emphatic Baltimore blowouts. TOP PICK Ravens vs Browns player prop: Derrick Henry Over 88.5 rushing yards The Ravens have handed Henry a heavy workload once again this season - he leads the league with 113 carries while averaging 95.2 YPG on the ground, and yet there's room for more with Jackson sidelined. This AFC North duel is a favorable matchup for King Henry, too, with the Browns giving up 134 rushing yards last weekend in New York and dealing with injuries across the defensive line . I don't see that banged-up unit being a match for Baltimore's powerhouse RB, who sits third in the NFL in yards after contact (262). Henry has gone past this O/U number in eight of his last 10 outings , and a run-heavy script should produce 20+ carries. Ravens vs Browns combo The Ravens have scored 24+ points in each of their wins this year , and this line feels too low despite Jackson being sidelined. The Over is 7-3 in Baltimore's last 10 games, and it's been a winning ticket in the past five meetings between these teams . With Cleveland sweating on the health of key defensive playmakers, Huntley can deliver a similar stat line to his SNF effort against the Falcons (201 passing yards, two TD passes, no turnovers), while the Browns' offense is boosted by KC Concepcion clearing the concussion protocol. When Baltimore isn't riding Henry and the ground game, look for Mark Andrews to be a key checkdown option for Huntley. Andrews has 22 catches through five contests, and he's finished with 6+ targets in four of those outings . Ravens moneyline Mark Andrews Over 3.5 receptions Ravens vs Browns touchdown scorer: Harold Fannin Jr. The Browns feel likelier to have success through the air than on the ground on Sunday, and Harold Fannin Jr. stands out as an anytime TD pick after grabbing three scores already this year . Baltimore has given up three touchdowns to tight ends in the opening five weeks , and snap count shouldn't be an issue for Fannin Jr. after logging a 93% mark last weekend against the Jets. With Concepcion and Denzel Boston occupying the Ravens' secondary, look for Fannin Jr. to thrive on underneath routes. His 6-foot-4 frame is ideal for red-zone jump balls. Want more NFL player props? away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out
away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about the defender, saying he is excited to get him back out on the field. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up for their divisional matchup with their former offensive coordinator-turned-head coach, Todd Monken, and his Cleveland Browns. The full final injury report is as follows: Jackson is still dealing with his sprained ankle and will now miss his second consecutive game. Joining Jackson is rookie tight end Matt Hibner, who suffered a hand injury. Reports indicate that Hibner has a cast on his hand, pointing to what could be a significant injury. There are no other red flags unless Jones or Vorhees are both unable to play, which would put the Baltimore offensive line in a very tough spot.

The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle), who didn't practice Thursday or Friday. He has six tackles so far this season. Minter also ruled out Cam Jurgens (concussion) for Sunday's game, meaning rookie Vega Ioane will get another start at center.. The Ravens also have other offensive line injuries to monitor with guards Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) both questionable to play. They were limited throughout the week. Wide receivers Zay Flowers (toe) and Rashod Bateman (shoulder) are good to go with no injury designation. Flowers was limited Thursday and Friday but Bateman returned to full participation. Rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane could return from injured reserve after he suffered a wrist injury in Week 1 in Indianapolis. Lane had three full days of practice this week and is listed as questionable. He would have to be removed from injured reserve this weekend to play. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. Gardner left the game during Tennessee’s opening possession of the second half after experiencing discomfort in his left leg. According to ESPN’s Stephen Holder, Gardner requested to leave the field before trainers began examining his left calf. The two-time All-Pro was subsequently taken to the locker room for further evaluation. The Colts held a 13-3 lead when Gardner exited during the third quarter. Gardner’s injury raises concerns for Colts defense Gardner eventually returned to the sideline and attempted to loosen up his injured leg, although his availability for the remainder of the contest remained uncertain. Cam Taylor-Britt replaced Gardner at outside cornerback, leaving Indianapolis without its top defensive back. The injury is particularly concerning because Gardner previously experienced calf problems during the 2025 season. Those issues forced him to miss several games after joining Indianapolis in a blockbuster trade with the New York Jets . The Colts surrendered two first-round draft selections and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to acquire Gardner, demonstrating their commitment to strengthening the secondary. Gardner entered Sunday’s matchup having appeared in all six games this season. According to Colts Wire, opposing quarterbacks had completed nine of 17 passes targeting Gardner for 195 yards, while the veteran cornerback recorded three pass breakups. His ability to match up against opposing receivers makes him an important part of Indianapolis’ defensive strategy. Losing Gardner for an extended period could force the Colts to make significant adjustments in coverage, particularly against teams featuring explosive passing attacks. However, the immediate concern is determining the severity of his latest injury. away.headline: Patriots injury report: 2 players out vs. Jets, plus latest on AJ Brown
away.blurb: New England ruled two players out for Week 6, and they both field the same position: cornerback. Although they’ll miss two with Davis and Prunty out again against the Jets, they’re officially getting their star back in Christian Gonzalez after he missed the last two contests with a shoulder injury. Although the CB room is looking better, there’s a chance the Patriots’ secondary could be a bit thin once more. Rookie CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) were both deemed questionable. Canada has missed the last two games and was limited during all three practices this week. Woodson, who played 50 snaps last week, was a full participant on Friday. Running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and starting left tackle Will Campbell (knee) were ruled questionable for Sunday after each sustained injuries during the Week 5 victory. The pair were limited during all three practices. The long-awaited return of star wide receiver A.J. Brown could be happening as soon as Sunday at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots ruled him questionable to play after he returned to practice this week for the first time since injuring his ankle in Week 1 and landing on IR. Brown has missed the last four games, which is the minimum amount of time required to miss for a player on IR. His return to practice on Wednesday meant he could be activated to the 53-man roster at any time. “We’ll have to see how he responds from practice today and then go from there,” Vrabel said. Brown was ultimately limited during Friday’s practice, as he was on Wednesday and Thursday. But Brown, who the Patriots traded for from the Philadelphia Eagles over the summer, gives the offense plenty more size and a veteran presence, two things any team hoping to return to the Super Bowl for a second consecutive season needs long-term at the position. The post Patriots injury report: 2 players out vs. Jets, plus latest on A.J. Brown appeared first on Boston.com . away.headline: New York Jets May Face A.J. Brown in New England Patriots Game - Report
away.blurb: Brown was listed as questionable on the Patriots injury report, and the team has not yet officially confirmed his return. If he does play, he opens up a major downfield threat for the Patriots. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye got off to a bad start this season, with just one touchdown pass in the first three games to go with six interceptions. But he rallied to form in back-to-back wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders, racking up 643 passing yards to go with seven touchdowns against just one interception. Brown’s return would likely open up even more possibilities. The New York Jets’ chances of an upset win against the New England Patriots may get harder if an expected personnel move comes to fruition. A source told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that star receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated by the Patriots in time for Sunday’s game against the Jets. Brown missed the last four games with a high ankle sprain on his right leg. Brown, 29 years old, is a three-time Pro Bowl receiver. He was acquired from the Eagles in the offseason for a 2028 first-round draft pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. Brown caught three passes for 26 yards in the Patriots opener on Sept. 9 against the Seattle Seahawks. He suffered a high ankle sprain in the third quarter, and the Patriots went on to lose 13-10 in a rematch of last season’s Super Bowl teams. In Brown’s absence, the Patriots made do with a receiving corps featuring Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. “We’ve got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it’s going to be tough on defenses,” Maye said earlier this week. “But I know we’ve got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it.” The Jets and Patriots will square off at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Massachusetts. The Patriots are currently 7.5 point favorites.

home.blurb: New England ruled two players out for Week 6, and they both field the same position: cornerback. home.blurb: The New England Patriots added a pair of key players to their growing list of injury concerns during their blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday as running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell each exited and did not return. The team has also been shorthanded at wide receiver. Offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's season opener and hasn't played since, though according to multiple reports he could be nearing a return. In addition, Mack Hollins was placed on injured reserve with a calf injury he suffered against the Bills. October 13, 2026 / 2:41 PM EDT / CBS Boston On Tuesday, NFL insiders provided updates on both Henderson and Campbell's injuries. Of the pair, the news was worse for Henderson. According to Adam Schefter of ESPN , the running back suffered a high ankle sprain in the second quarter of Sunday's game and is expected to miss multiple weeks. According to Schefter, Henderson will not require surgery and the team is hoping he will be back "relatively soon." The news was slightly better for Campbell, whose right knee got rolled up on, also in the second quarter. It was the same knee that Campbell hurt last year. Last season, he was placed on injured reserve. When he returned to action, Campbell wasn't the same player for the stretch run as New England made it all the way to the Super Bowl. Following Sunday's injury, Tom Pelissero reported that Campbell avoided a major knee injury. The NFL insider reported that Campbell is considered week-to-week. Rookie first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu would likely replace Campbell at left tackle should he be forced to miss time. Lomu came in following Campbell's injury and performed well against the Raiders. The Patriots have won back-to-back games despite a growing injury list. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez missed both games, and fellow defensive back Carlton Davis joined him as inactive against the Raiders. Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked after Sunday's game how the team has embraced the next man up mentality. "Because that's what it has to be. You know what I mean? It's, we try not to panic," Vrabel said. "We just try to get the next guy ready. We ask everybody to prepare as a starter, so credit to the football players, you know, particularly the guys on this team, uh, the guys that we've tried to bring in here. And they realize that when you get an opportunity and you do something with it, then you get more opportunities." How do the Patriots continue to overcome injuries to rack up wins?

The Saints have the league’s 20th-ranked offense (322.0 yards per game) and the 25th-ranked defense (361.0 yards per game) as they head into MetLife Stadium against a Giants team that has a chance to go 4-0 at home for the first time since 2008, when they got off to a 6-0 start at home. Despite the Saints’ struggles, they enter this game as a 1.5-point favorite per FanDuel , which is a head-scratcher considering they have averaged 21.3 points in their last three games, while the home team has averaged 25 points per game. But odds aside, the NFC East-leading Giants’ goal, according to head coach John Harbaugh, is simple: stack wins. “You always know what they are, but you know you’ve got to stack wins to make the December standings matter,” Harbaugh said when asked how much he pays attention to the standings at this point in the season. “So, we focus on the next game.” The Giants, according to Tankathon , have to make hay, so to speak. They face a remaining schedule with a combined winning percentage of .484, with their four toughest opponents being the 49ers, Jaguars, Lions, and Browns. All four of those challenging opponents land on the schedule after the Giants’ Week 8 bye. But to focus on what the Giants might do this week, let’s look at the best- and worst-case scenarios. Why the Giants Will Beat the Saints Oct 11, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) runs the ball during the third quarter against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. It also ranks last in the league in defensive rush success (52.5%), meaning it struggles to stop opponents from gaining the minimum required yardage on a run (excluding kneeldowns and scrambles). The Giants’ rushing offense has not been the same since quarterback Jaxson Dart landed on IR with a season-ending knee injury. Although it ranks 17th in total rushing yards, it also averages a dismal 3.7 yards per attempt, 24th in the league. As if the rushing game’s struggles aren’t enough, it will be interesting to see if Harbaugh decides to reduce running back Cam Skattebo’s touches this week given his fumbling issue. As usual, the head coach was mum on the plans, but this could be a week when Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. get bigger roles in the rushing attack to see if they can jumpstart it. On the defensive side, the Giants’ pass rush has finally awakened after a slow start, recording seven sacks over the last two weeks. This week, they face a Saints offensive line that has surrendered three sacks to quarterback Tyler Shough over that same period. Combine that with the opportunistic Giants secondary, which has forced eight turnovers this season , against a Saints offense that has committed 13 giveaways, and the Giants’ quest to remain undefeated at home could get a lot easier. Why the Giants Won’t Beat the Saints Oct 5, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) scores a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Caesars Superdome. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. There are many reasons for the Giants’ struggles in run defense, but one glaring issue has been facing pre-snap motion. Motion changes the look for the defense and has sometimes left players out of position or forced them into bad angles as they try to stop the play from gaining a lot of yards. Under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints have deployed pre-snap motion on 64% of their offensive snaps this season, the ninth-highest rate in the league, and have a 46% success rate overall when using motion. While they use pre-snap motion more in the passing game, they have used it at a 35% rate in the rushing game. If the Giants, who have allowed opponents 5.2 yards per rush attempt on first down, can’t tighten that up, the Saints will have options on subsequent downs, giving New Orleans an advantage. The other thing that could spoil the Giants’ quest to win their fourth straight game at home is their own aggressiveness on defense. If the Giants, who over the last two weeks have blitzed on 57.8% of opposing quarterbacks’ drop backs, come at the Saints with a similar rate of pressure, they’d better hope that Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough, who per PFF data, has a 102.7 passer rating when throwing the ball in 2.5 seconds or less, doesn’t connect with receivers Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed for the big pass plays downfield. If I live to be 100 (fingers crossed), I will never understand how the oddsmakers come up with their weekly point spreads. What I do understand is that Harbaugh has this team dialed in, and this matchup against the Saints is overall favorable for the Giants if they play a relatively clean game and keep the ball-security issues out of the mix. The Giants have a lot more going for them at this point in the season than the Saints, including far too many advantages that, if they hit on all cylinders, will get the job done. Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore. The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences. With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East. Here are our predictions for Sunday's game. Grant Chachere, Staff Writer: L 24-17 This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis . I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth. While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints. At the half, join us for Halftime Studs & Duds . Then, a fter the game, join us for our Biggest Winners & Biggest Losers , our View of the Game , and the Most Important Quotes from Kellen Moore & Players . Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble. I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out. Prediction: Giants 24, Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 21-17 Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three? We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust. Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are. Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. However, don't bet the house on who I choose to win today. I've only been right once in five prognostications this year. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Saints are 1.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 45.5 total points. New Orleans is a -115 moneyline favorite to win outright, while New York is listed as a -105 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Saints vs Giants predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 18. Saints vs Giants pick: Saints -1.5 (+100) My Giants vs. Saints best bet is New Orleans to cover the spread (-1.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel . Saints vs Giants Odds for NFL Week 6 Saints vs Giants spread: Saints -1.5, Giants +1.5 Saints vs Giants total: over/under 45.5 Saints vs Giants moneyline: Saints -115, Giants -105 New Orleans Saints vs New York Giants Preview The Saints originally opened as underdogs for this game, but almost immediately swung to 1.5-point road favorites — and I think they are sitting at the absolute bottom of their market value. Am I thrilled to back New Orleans on the road here? Not exactly. But I am itching to fade the Giants . Sure, the Saints' run defense is abysmal, but they are facing a Giants team entirely incapable of exploiting it. New Orleans has played a grueling schedule the last two weeks, facing the Falcons (who ran wild with Bijan Robinson) and the Vikings (who have one of the best defenses in the NFL). Offensively, Tyler Shough has been very good when kept clean in the pocket. With the Giants missing Brian Burns , Shough should have all day to operate and consistently move the ball through the air in this game. The Giants are a couple games above .500, but they are arguably the most fraudulent team in the NFL. They could easily be 1-4 right now after lucking out with a tie against the Commanders last week. New York's back-to-back home wins came against the Titans and Cardinals — two incompetent teams that turned the ball over at the goal line with a chance to win. Offensively, the Giants have completely stalled since losing Jaxson Dart. They rank 29th in both rush success rate and rush EPA, meaning their ground game has almost totally vanished. Jameis Winston has thrown for 694 yards with a 6:3 TD:INT ratio in the three games he's started. He's done a good job of feeding Malik Nabers as the Giants' WR1 has surpassed 100 receiving yards in each of the last two weeks. Of course, the thing with Winston is that he's prone to making critical mistakes when throwing into zone coverage. Saints vs Giants Pick, Betting Analysis There is a massive strength-of-schedule disparity here, with the Giants feasting on the easiest schedule in the league so far while the Saints have been heavily battle tested against some of the NFL's best. Without Jaxson Dart's mobility, the Giants simply haven't bee able to run the ball with Cam Skattebo, forcing Jameis Winston into high-variance, mistake-prone dropbacks. The Saints should be able to keep the pocket clean for Tyler Shough throughout this game, which will likely allow him to dissect the Giants' defense and lift his team to a road win. away.headline: New Orleans Saints declare multiple players out, top New York Giants players questionable for Week 6 matchup
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The New Orleans Saints have concluded their week of practice leading up to their Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants. New Orleans declared two players out, and a few more are questionable. Starting linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf), and backup EDGE Anfernee Jennings (knee) have each been declared out for Sunday’s game in East Rutherford. Both players will miss their third-straight games. Running back Alvin Kamara (back), wide receiver Chris Olave (illness), defensive tackle Nathan Shepard (illness), and safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) were all limited Friday and are questionable to play. Olave and Shepard were DNPs for most of the week, so it’s good that they at least got some practice time in before the weekend. Long snapper Zach Wood (calf) is also questionable, though he was a full participant all week in practice. He still needs to be activated off the Reserve/Injured list. Starting EDGE Abdul Carter (calf), starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and starting left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) are all officially questionable to face the Saints. They were all limited Friday, giving them at least a chance to suit up. Starting cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) starting safety Tyler Nubin (neck) have been declared out, making the Giants secondary depleted. Tight end Theo Johnson (neck) is also out after not practicing Friday. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports.
