home.headline: New York Giants' Latest Injury Concern is Beyond Terrifying
home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season The New York Giants have dealt with enough injury issues this year. Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns are both out for the season. Andrew Thomas is nursing a groin issue. Jermaine Eluemunor just hurt his calf. The secondary is banged up. Abdul Carter did not practice on Wednesday due to a calf injury, and while head coach John Harbaugh said Carter is "doing very well," it's hard not to be worried. Harbaugh doesn't sound too concerned, so hopefully, it's just something minor and Carter is being held out as a precautionary measure. New York Giants' Latest Injury Concern is Beyond Terrifying - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New York Giants' Latest Injury Concern is Beyond Terrifying (Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads But just when you thought it couldn't get any worse for the Giants, another alarming injury concern popped up on Wednesday. Calf issues can be tricky, and for a player like Carter who relies heavily on his explosiveness and burst, it can become a very serious problem. But the Giants are already without Burns, and Kayvon Thibodeaux has been a non-factor through the first five games. The last thing New York's ailing pass rush needs is for Carter to be sidelined, too. Carter has logged two sacks and six quarterback hits thus far, so it's not like he's been a game-wrecker. But he has been, by far, the Giants' best pass rusher, and he was No. 3 overall pick in 2025 for a reason. New York has managed just eight sacks as a team heading into Week 6, which ranks toward the bottom of the NFL. Obviously, losing Burns — who racked up 16.5 sacks a year ago — is devastating. But the Giants should still be generating more pressure with Carter and Thibodeaux than they have. It would certainly help if Thibodeaux were more effective . The 25-year-old has posted six tackles and no sacks, and his lone quarterback hit came back in Week 1. You would never know this is the same Thibodeaux that rattled off 11.5 sacks in 2023 and appeared to be an up-and-coming star at the time. For now, though, the Giants absolutely Carter on the field, not just because Thibodeaux has been struggling, but because Carter is supposed to be New York's next star defender. Carter was one of five Giants players to miss practice Wednesday, with Thomas, Eluemunor, Colton Hood and Tyler Nubin being the others. New York will be hosting the 1-4 New Orleans Saints this Sunday and will have a brilliant opportunity to improve to 4-1-1 and bolster its standing at the top of the NFC East. Hopefully, Carter is able to take the gridiron for Big Blue.

home.headline: New Orleans Saints declare multiple players out, top New York Giants players questionable for Week 6 matchup
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: The New Orleans Saints have concluded their week of practice leading up to their Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants. New Orleans declared two players out, and a few more are questionable. Starting linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf), and backup EDGE Anfernee Jennings (knee) have each been declared out for Sunday’s game in East Rutherford. Both players will miss their third-straight games. Running back Alvin Kamara (back), wide receiver Chris Olave (illness), defensive tackle Nathan Shepard (illness), and safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) were all limited Friday and are questionable to play. Olave and Shepard were DNPs for most of the week, so it’s good that they at least got some practice time in before the weekend. Long snapper Zach Wood (calf) is also questionable, though he was a full participant all week in practice. He still needs to be activated off the Reserve/Injured list. Starting EDGE Abdul Carter (calf), starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and starting left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) are all officially questionable to face the Saints. They were all limited Friday, giving them at least a chance to suit up. Starting cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) starting safety Tyler Nubin (neck) have been declared out, making the Giants secondary depleted. Tight end Theo Johnson (neck) is also out after not practicing Friday. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. away.headline: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return
away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. The Eagles already ruled Hurts out when they announced the starting quarterback is dealing with a "superficial blood clot." It's unclear how much time Hurts will miss; estimates seem to vary from as little as a couple weeks to as most as a season-ending issue. We all hope the best for Hurts' health while he recovers. In the meantime, Tanner McKee will start at quarterback. It seems like Cole Payton will serve as the backup QB while new addition Joe Milton III could be the emergency third option, at least for Sunday's game. Barkley is missing his second straight game due to a hamstring injury. With Barkley out and now both Tank Bigsby and Shipley on injured reserve, the Eagles have two health running backs on their roster: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. Look for Pierce to start while Steele could be mixed in. The Eagles also have Jaydon Blue and Ian Wheeler on the practice squad if they want to use a temporary elevation for more backfield depth. The Eagles ruled one player DOUBTFUL: A.J. Epenesa. Epenesa was limited on Wednesday before being downgraded to not practicing on Thursday and Friday. With Hunt out and Epenesa likely not playing, the Eagles will be without two of their five edge rushers. The Eagles ruled five players QUESTIONABLE: Landon Dickerson, Drew Kendall, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, and Jakorian Bennett. Dickerson was limited in practice all week. I have a hard time believing the Eagles will activate him from injured to play before he's able to fully participate in at least one practice. Kendall missed Wednesday's practice before being limited on Thursday and Friday. Doesn't seem conducive to him suiting up on Sunday. If neither Dickerson nor Kendall play, the Eagles will likely use their same starting offensive line from last week: LT Jordan Mailata, LG Willie Lampkin, C Jake Majors, RG Tyler Steen, RT Markel Bell. Continuity!!!!! The big news is that DeVonta is returning to the field after missing the Eagles' last two games due to a hamstring injury. The Eagles ramped DeVonta up this week from not practicing on Wednesday to being limited on Thursday to being full on Friday. The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers. As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Steelers 24, Bucs 20 The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers. I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays. I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win. Overall Record: 3-2 James Hill, Writer: Steelers 21, Bucs 17 I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend. Overall record: 2-3 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 21, Steelers 14 So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week. Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon. Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win. Logan Robinson, Founder: Steelers 31, Bucs 24 This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh. I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season. I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter. River Wells, Editor: Steelers 24, Bucs 17 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better. The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters. On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too. The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it. Consensus: Steelers 4, Bucs 1 The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year? away.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy misses halftime after on-field injury
away.blurb: "He went right into the blue medical tent, and he spent the entire halftime in the tent. He just came out. He never went to the locker room at halftime as he was getting his leg looked at." Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy coached the second half of his team's NFL Week 6 game against Tampa Bay with a foot injury. The 62-year-old told reporters after his team's 26-19 victory that his foot was stepped on leading up to halftime. The CBS broadcast reported that the 62-year-old spent halftime in the blue medical tent on the Steelers' sideline instead of joining his team in the locker room. He was seen limping on the field at Raymond James Stadium, favoring his right foot. "Mike McCarthy, heading off the field, and appears to have twisted his ankle," CBS play-by-play announcer Andrew Catalon observed as the broadcast returned from studio coverage at the half. "You can see him slow up, and then needing a little assistance. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. What happened to Mike McCarthy? CBS sideline reporter AJ Ross called the injury a "freak thing" as McCarthy was walking to speak with her at halftime. Cameras did not capture exactly what happened, but he told reporters that the discomfort was caused by being stepped on and not by rolling his ankle. The veteran is in his first season as coach of his hometown team after 18 seasons with Green Bay and Dallas. He is the offense's play-caller, so any departure from the playing surface would have been a change to the team's process. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers said afterward that the injury disrupted little about the team's routine, though there was concern among players. "There wasn't a whole lot different at halftime," Rodgers said. "It was still the same chaos, but people said Mike didn't come in and people were wondering what the heck's going on. Is he OK? Glad he's OK." Cameras showed McCarthy standing on the sideline throughout the second half, so the mishap did not appear to impact his ability to stay involved in the game. His offense rallied from a 13-3 halftime deficit to tie the game late in the fourth quarter, then win in overtime. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he's caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who's handled a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence. home.headline: Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield may try to return from injury for Panthers game
home.blurb: It sounds like Mayfield could attempt to return to the lineup when the Buccaneers play at the 3-2 Carolina Panthers on Oct. 25. Bowles previously said that Mayfield would likely be sidelined for "a minimum of three weeks" due to his setback, but a subsequent report noted that the signal-caller wanted to return after just two missed games. Such a scenario didn't play out, but Ira Kaufman of the JoeBucsFan website noted on Monday that "even Baker Mayfield detractors can’t muster a sensible argument to keep him sidelined once he is healed from a dislocated right thumb" following what happened at Tampa Bay's Raymond James Stadium on Sunday afternoon. A Tampa Bay Buccaneers side that has been without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield since he went down with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand in Week 3 fell to 1-5 on the season when it squandered a 16-3 lead en route to suffering a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Buccaneers will evaluate Baker Mayfield "during the week" ahead of Panthers game Per Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles confirmed on Monday that Mayfield is on track to practice this coming Wednesday. "He’s supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said about Mayfield. "We’re gonna take a good look at him there, and we’ll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does." U ndrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has served as Tampa Bay's temporary QB1 since the club's Week 4 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Oct. 4. While Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown to help Tampa Bay earn a stunning 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 8, he came back down to earth when he tossed a pair of interceptions and took five sacks in the Buccaneers' loss to the Steelers. Buccaneers will try to get Baker Mayfield, Jalon Daniels ready for Panthers game "Both will be in the meetings, obviously," Bowles added about Mayfield and Daniels. "Both will be in the meetings, and we’ll see how the week goes before we decide who it is." Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. home.headline: Rams Kicker Blake Grupe's Updated Injury Timeline After Replacing 'Thiccer Kicker' Harrison Mevis
home.blurb: Blake Grupe—who was signed this week to replace Harrison Mevis—suffered a knee injury during Sunday's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals while covering a kickoff. He was officially placed on injured reserve on Monday, ruling him out for at least four weeks. Bleacher Report • 8h Hunter's Wife Calls Out Sharpe The Los Angeles Rams have a kicker problem. Kyren Addresses Playing Time 😒 Mevis was just 5-for-9 on field goals this season, which included a miss and blocked attempt during last week's 37-34 overtime loss against the Buffalo Bills. His release didn't come as a major surprise. Special teams have been an issue for the Rams in general—last season, head coach Sean McVay fired special-teams coordinator Chase Blackburn late in the season after gaffes from that unit contributed to a number of losses. "This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of," McVay said of his special teams' group this season. "We'll lean in. We'll go back to work. We'll use these as growth opportunities." Grupe, 27, was expected to upgrade the kicker position. He started his career with the New Orleans Saints (2023-25) before a five-game stint with the Indianapolis Colts last season, where he was 11-for-11 on field goals and 10-for-10 on extra points. For his career he's 86-for-105 on field goals. "Those five weeks in Indy were seriously big for me, big for my career," he told reporters this past week. "I was able to get the ball rolling and show what I can do, and that was big for me." But the Colts gave the starting kicker position back to the previously injured Spencer Shrader over the summer and released Grupe, who then picked up with the New York Jets on their practice squad before the Rams signed him this week. Unfortunately for both Grupe and the Rams, injury very quickly struck. It had an immediate impact on Sunday—after scoring their first touchdown, the team went for a two-point try instead of kicking and failed to convert. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group. With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like. Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season. If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe. Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances. Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters. Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles. This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender. The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart. The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising. Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment. away.headline: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh provides injury updates on key players ahead of Week 6

As for Bud Dupree, Harbaugh listed him as day-to-day, while Tre' Harris and Donte Jackson are week-to-week. Dupree injured his neck in the third quarter against the Broncos. A day after their Week 5 loss, Jim Harbaugh provided injury updates on key players, including Ladd McConkey. Harbaugh said they were using McConkey as an emergency option, and he’s hopeful that he can practice this week. Harbaugh also provided an update on offensive guard Kayode Awosika, saying that he is healing and rehabbing. Awosika has missed the last three games with a lower leg injury. home.headline: Latest injury update on Kansas City Chiefs’ Josh Simmons, Jaylon Moore raises big offensive tackle questions for Week 7 vs. Seahawks
home.blurb: Leading into Week 6, the Chiefs had starting left tackle Josh Simmons back at practice in a limited capacity for all three sessions . Before last week, Simmons hadn't practiced since Aug. 16. Asked about his potential status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Reid was hesitant to overpromise. The team will continue to ramp up Simmons' workload and see how he responds as he returns from injury. The Chiefs could realistically be without two of their most experienced offensive tackles, Moore and Simmons. That would leave Kahlil Benson as the starting left tackle and Joshua Ezeudu as the starting right tackle. Diego Pounds would also be active for the first time since Kansas City acquired him in a trade , should Moore be out with his concussion. Reid discussed Ezeudu's Week 6 performance on Monday. The trade acquisition filled in for Moore after the concussion just before halftime against the Chargers. “I appreciated the guys and how they played yesterday,” Reid said “Josh (Ezeudu) jumped in and played at the right tackle spot. I thought he did a nice job there. So, and he's got experience. I'm not real worried about all that.” In 17 pass-blocking snaps on Sunday , Ezeudu allowed just one hurry per Pro Football Focus. The Chiefs put him in a good spot to be successful in that game. With a full week of practice and preparation as a potential starter, Ezeudu could deliver an even better performance against Seattle. Moore could realistically practice and play this week. It's not out of the question. It's happened before. However, concussions typically mean that you're slated to miss at least one week of the season. An independent neurologist must clear him before he can return to play. During the game, Kelce fell to the ground, and it appeared he turned his right ankle on a tackle from Daiyan Henley. Later, cameras caught Kelce on the sidelines getting his ankle looked at, worked on and taped. The NFL on CBS Sports shared the moment on X , but ultimately, Kelce stayed in for the rest of the game. The Chiefs won it, 22-6 . But after the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid admitted that Kelce was playing through an injury. Andy Reid confirms Travis Kelce played through an ankle injury Speaking with reporters after the game, Reid spoke about the team's injuries. "Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Jaylon Moore has a concussion, Travis Kelce played through an ankle injury, Jalen Royals was checked for a concussion but he was OK and Kingsley Suamataia got kicked in the calf," Chiefs beat writer Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star shared on social media. So, Kelce is definitely injured, although Reid didn't offer many details about the extent of the injury. Former NFL team doctor David Chao took to X during the game, however, to give his take on the injury based on what he saw on camera. home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston off report vs. Chiefs
home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were both completely taken off the injury report and should be ready to roll against the Chiefs. Fellow wideouts KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Brenen Thompson were both listed as questionable but both should also be in line to return to the field, though KLS still needs to be activated officially off of IR before Sunday. The other players listed as questionable are defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell, edge rusher Bud Dupree, linebacker Daiyan Henley, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is the lone player with a doubtful tag. Offensive tackle Joe Alt, guard Kayode Awosika, wide receiver Tre' Harris, cornerback Donte Jackson, and safety Derwin James were all ruled out for Sunday. This will be the third missed game for James and the second missed game for Alt who is still receiving opinions on his neck injury he sustained against the Seahawks. *Note that Bud Dupree is listed as both questionable and out. We'll wait for further clarification before adjusting the report. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their final injury report ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Speaking to the media on Friday afternoon, Chiefs HC Andy Reid ruled out WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) and LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 6. Rice did not participate in practice this week; however, he was seen on the sideline coaching up second-year WR Jalen Royals. Simmons was a limited participant all week, which Coach Reid said was intentional. “Yeah, he got some work,” Reid said. “He didn't work in the team periods, but that was the idea that we went out with, just so we could get some base in there with some fundamentals and technique and start getting that back.” Simmons continues to make incremental strides toward returning after missing practically two months with a bulging disc in his back. “Yeah, he was excited to be out there,” Reid said of Simmons. “Just be back with the guys and out there on the field, instead of the meeting room.” Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's final Week 6 injury report, including game-status designations. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. However, the Raiders have surprised everyone and started the season 3-0. Their hot start has cooled down a bit, thanks to facing some heavy hitters in the conference. They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3. Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8. Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league. Bills vs. Raiders: where to watch Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 4:25 p.m. ET Location: Allegiant Stadium (Las Vegas) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -5.5 ( via DraftKings ) Bills vs. Raiders prediction The Raiders were put in a difficult stretch, facing the Chiefs, Patriots and Bills back-to-back-to-back. While Vegas got off to a solid start this season, I think their recent stretch is a bit too much for them to attack. I think the last two losses may be hard to shake off. I think the Bills will start to shake off their ball security problems and Allen just seems to be unstoppable, even when he is committing turnovers. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

away.headline: Buffalo Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson suspended without pay by the NFL over spitting shame
away.blurb: Gardner-Johnson will be eligible to return to the Bills roster on November 2 after missing the team's game against the Baltimore Ravens , though there is still the potential for Buffalo to issue further punishment to their player. Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game without pay by the NFL over his shameful spitting incident against the Las Vegas Raiders. Gardner-Johnson has since offered a groveling apology for the disgusting moment, in which cameras caught him approaching Raiders tight end Brock Bowers for a heated exchange of words – before spitting in his rival's direction. The shocking moment occurred right in front of an official, who quickly flagged the action. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game soon after and left the field with a bizarre grin on his face. The NFL took less than 24 hours to make its decision on a punishment, releasing a statement to the media on Monday afternoon over the 'act of unsportsmanlike conduct.' The league claims Gardner-Johnson 'violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."' The NFL adds: 'Under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, Gardner-Johnson may appeal the suspension. Any appeal will be heard and decided upon by either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera, or James Thrash, the hearing officers jointly appointed and compensated by the NFL and NFLPA to decide appeals of on-field player discipline.' After the spitting incident on Sunday, the 28-year-old posted a lengthy apology on his Instagram story. He wrote: 'I want to take a moment to address my actions and sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me. 'My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed. The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game.' He continued: 'There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard. 'To my opponent, I sincerely apologize. We compete hard between those lines, but respect should always remain at the forefront. C.J. I will learn from this, grow from it, and continue to lead with the integrity, passion, and respect that have carried me throughout my career. home.blurb: The news comes just one day after questions surfaced about whether Las Vegas would consider resting Jeanty to allow his injuries additional time to heal. However, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak quickly dismissed that possibility Wednesday, making it clear that the team expects its starting running back to be available against Buffalo. Jeanty was listed as questionable against New England after missing Friday's practice but was ultimately cleared to participate. However, his production was limited in the Raiders' 45-17 loss. Although injuries have limited his effectiveness this season, the Raiders continue to view him as a central piece of their offensive plans. His availability becomes even more important as Las Vegas prepares to face a Buffalo team entering Week 6 with a 4-1 record. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. After spending much of the season dealing with foot and ankle injuries, the second-year running back appears to be making significant progress. Speaking with reporters at his locker Thursday, Jeanty said he was feeling great and that this was the best he had felt all season, according to ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. "He's playing," Kubiak said when asked about potentially sitting Jeanty. Kubiak also noted that Jeanty was making progress in his recovery, raising the possibility that he could take on a larger workload during practice. Jeanty's comments Thursday offered further encouragement, suggesting that the running back is beginning to feel more comfortable after battling injuries throughout the season. The former Boise State standout first suffered an ankle injury during training camp in August. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

Gardner-Johnson (22) during an NFL football game in Las Vegas, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. Credit: AP/David Becker ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardiner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardiner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardiner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” Buffalo Bills running back Ty Johnson (26) runs past Buffalo Bills running back Ray Davis (7) after making a catch during an NFL football game in Las Vegas, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious. New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers. Cowboys vs. Packers prediction Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams . However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. The Cowboys are averaging 3.07 points per drive, the second-highest by a team under .500 through five games this century per CBS Sports Research, but their 45 drives this season are the second fewest in the league this season. Among the NFL teams that have played in all five weeks of the 2026 season, Dallas' 45 drives stand as the fewest. That's what happens when you have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed). LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. picks.blurb: Who Experts Are Picking For Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers in Week 6 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers enter their Week 6 contest at Lambeau Field on Sunday night coming off very different Week 5 showings. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. Sports Illustrated Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) and Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur against the Chicago Bears during their football at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Wm. Glasheen USAToday Network via IMAGN images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Albert Breer: Packers Eva Geitheim: Packers Mitch Goldich: Packers Mike Kadlick: Packers Gilberto Manzano: Packers Conor Orr: Packers John Pluym: Packers Matt Verderame: Packers Iain MacMillan: Packers Peter Dewey: Packers Albert Breer: Packers Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Ceedee Lamb (88) before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Bowen: Packers Mike Clay: Packers Jeremy Fowler: Cowboys Dan Graziano: Packers Kalyn Kahler: Packers Pamela Maldonado: Cowboys Eric Moody: Packers Jason Reid: Cowboys Ben Solak: Cowboys Lindsey Thiry: Packers Seth Wickersham: Packers Matt Bowen: Packers Week 5: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson does a Lambeau Leap after scoring a touchdown against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. The Packers defeated the Bears, 31-7. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Pete Prisco: Packers Jared Dubin: Packers Ryan Wilson: Packers John Breech: Cowboys Tyler Sullivan: Cowboys Dave Richard: Packers Jamey Eisenberg: Packers Pete Prisco: Packers Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) celebrates during the game between the Cowboys and the Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jeremy Bergman: Packers Brooke Cersosimo: Packers Gennaro Filice: Packers Bobby Kownack: Cowboys Dan Parr: Packers Jeremy Bergman: Packers Final expert tally and my prediction Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Packers: 26 The biggest problem for the Cowboys in this game is Green Bay's ability to move the ball through the air . The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. away.headline: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report
away.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status
