away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender Skip to main content SI.COM As if everything else that has gone wrong for the Dallas Cowboys' defense hasn't been enough, the unit has also been ravaged by injuries to make matters worse. The Cowboys are missing starters at cornerback, safety and linebacker, and now they are in danger of losing yet another linebacker from the starting lineup. Dee Winters, KaVontae Turpin injury updates Dallas Cowboys wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (9) returns a punt against the Houston Texans during the first half at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Winters is actually dealing with an Achilles strain. Meanwhile, Turpin has a rib cartilage issue, with the good news being that X-Rays came back clean on the wideout's injury. After the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Winters is actually dealing with an Achilles strain. Meanwhile, Turpin has a rib cartilage issue, with the good news being that X-Rays came back clean on the wideout's injury. "Cowboys LB Dee Winters has an Achilles strain and WR KaVontae Turpin is dealing with a rib cartilage issue. X-rays clean," Nick Harris of the Forth Worth Star-Telegram relayed. There was some concern about Dak Prescott's ribs after he took a shot to the area during the game and seemed to favor them, but Schotty said he is not aware of the Cowboys quarterback receiving any X-rays , so Prescott seems to be OK. It isn't immediately clear if either player will miss time. At linebacker, Shemar James took over for Winters and finished with five tackles. When is DeMarvion Overshown coming back? Last Thursday did not go as planned for Dallas, as the team suffered an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home, but the team gets an opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 with another primetime showdown. This weekend, Dallas will make the trip to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night showdown with the Green Bay Packers . Along with Overshown, Miller, and Speed improving their participation statuses on Thursday, there was another player who took a positive step forward: star cornerback Joey Porter Jr ., whose home debut was spoiled last week after a sudden illness. But after some extra time to recover from the issues that left him throwing up in the locker room before being sent home , he is feeling well and on track to play on Sunday night. Porter was listed on Wednesday's report with an ankle issue, but it is not serious, and he will be in line for an increased workload this week. Per reports, Porter is expected to have a "near full workload" in Week 6 . Hopefully, everyone will continue improving as the week continues, with just two days remaining until game day. away.headline: Packers vs. Cowboys: Breaking down final injury report of Week 6
away.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. Receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) does not have an status designation and will play. How will the injury situation affect Sunday night's showdown with the Cowboys? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 6: OL Jacob Monk (quad): He's no longer a starting option at right guard, where Travis Glover or Kevin Zeitler will start Sunday, but Monk could be a backup at center and get snaps on special teams protection units if he's healthy. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): He only just returned to practice this week, and even though the Packers need help along the defensive line, Riley is unlikely to play Sunday. He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy. DL Javon Hargrave (Achilles): The veteran suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon injury last Sunday and will eventually go on injured reserve, possibly as soon as Saturday. home.blurb: Schefter went on to state that Parsons likely wouldn’t be back until at least early next month. His knee injury has kept him on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list the entire season. While it would have been quite the storyline if Parsons returned this past Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, his former team, his 21-day practice window still has not opened up. Before the ex-Cowboy can make his return, that window must open up. With a pivotal Sunday afternoon tilt against the Lions approaching, it sounds as if Parsons will continue his stint on the PUP. If Schefter’s timeline is correct, the earliest the Packers would get Parsons back could be in New England against the Patriots on November 8th. Green Bay’s bye is two weeks after that. It feels more likely that the former first-rounder will return against the Los Angeles Rams in a primetime matchup on Thanksgiving Eve. In any case, the sooner the Pack gets Parsons back, the better. Their postseason hopes may depend on it. At 4-2, the Green Bay Packers are tied with the Chicago Bears for second place in the NFC North. The duo are a game and a half behind the Minnesota Vikings at 5-0. Riding a three-game winning streak, the Packers will travel to Detroit to take on the Lions in a divisional clash. The Lions are right behind Green Bay at 3-2. They’ll also be fresh, coming off a bye week. While the Pack prepares for a pivotal matchup, they received an update on star edge rusher Micah Parsons . Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter on the Pat McAfee Show, Parsons is still at least a couple of weeks away from returning. McAfee shared Schefter’s report via X, formerly Twitter. “I was told that Micah Parsons wasn’t close to playing against the Dallas Cowboys,” Schefter said on the show. “They haven’t opened up his practice window yet, and I’m not anticipating that right now.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Like ClutchPoints’ content? home.headline: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report
home.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status

home.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. Receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) does not have an status designation and will play. How will the injury situation affect Sunday night's showdown with the Cowboys? He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy. DL Javon Hargrave (Achilles): The veteran suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon injury last Sunday and will eventually go on injured reserve, possibly as soon as Saturday. home.headline: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers
home.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday. Packers Rule Out Four, Including Javon Hargrave Green Bay ruled out defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave , receiver Skyy Moore , and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste . Defensive tackle Jordon Riley , who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, is doubtful with an Achilles injury. Guard Aaron Banks is questionable with a knee and toe injury, along with defensive tackle Anthony Campbell with an ankle injury, cornerback Brandon Cisse with a hip injury added Friday, center/guard Jacob Monk with a quadriceps injury, and receiver Savion Williams , who has an ankle injury and is also in his return window. ‘I Just Kept Throwing Up’: Joey Porter Jr. Details Illness That Kept Him Out Against Buccaneers, Targets Green Bay A New Ankle Listing For Joey Porter Jr. Full Go For CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Smith, And Alijah Clark Safety Alijah Clark , who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, practiced fully all three days and carries no game status. So did left tackle Tyler Guyton with a back injury, outside linebacker James Houston with a shoulder injury, receiver CeeDee Lamb with a thigh injury, cornerback Shavon Revel with a knee injury, and left guard Tyler Smith with his surgically repaired thumb. Lamb said Thursday that his thigh bruise started in the second quarter of the Cowboys’ win at Houston and that he was back to square one after the mini-bye. Cornerback Keisean Nixon , edge rusher Lukas Van Ness , safety Evan Williams , and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt carry no game status. Micah Parsons , who is recovering from a torn ACL, is not on the report. Kickoff at Lambeau Field is set for 7:20 p.m. CT on Sunday, Oct. 18, on NBC. Save my name, email, and website in

The San Francisco 49ers and Brock Purdy are looking to keep their undefeated season going when they host the Washington Commanders and former No. 2 overall pick Jayden Daniels. San Francisco upset the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5, and it has one of the best offenses in the league during this perfect 5-0 start. Purdy is gaining some MVP buzz, and the 49ers have battled through several major injuries to sit atop the NFC standings. Meanwhile, Washington tied the New York Giants in Week 5 after a late-game blunder led to the clock expiring on the team – in field goal range – in overtime. Daniels and the Commanders are now just 1-3-1 this season (0-2-1 when Daniels plays), and they need as many wins as they can get to remain in the mix to win the NFC East. The 49ers are considerable favorites in this game, and the total is one of the highest of the week at 50.5. In the leadup to this game, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player props selections and much more to help bettors get the most out of this matchup. I’ve decided to compile some of our favorite plays all into one spot ahead of Monday’s action. Here’s a breakdown of each of these bets – and their latest odds in the Commanders vs. 49ers matchup. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Commanders vs. 49ers Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook San Francisco 49ers -7.5 (-110) vs. Washington Commanders – Iain MacMillan Brock Purdy OVER 2.5 Passing Touchdowns (+146) – Peter Dewey Jayden Daniels OVER 36.5 Rushing Yards (-109) – Peter Dewey Mike Evans Anytime TD (-140) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . In Week 6, he’s taking the 49ers to cover at home: The only argument you can make to bet on the Commanders in this game, and it's not necessarily one that I'd disagree with, is that so many things have gone right for the 49ers through the first five weeks that they're bound to have a game where things go wrong. If that happens, and if Jayden Daniels can drag the Commanders' offense down the field enough, maybe Washington can cover this spread. With that being said, that's not enough for me to take the Commanders here, and considering I expect the line to shift even more towards San Francisco this week, I'll take them at -7.5 while I still can. There's a strong argument to be made that the 49ers are the best team in the NFL. They're second in net yards per play (+1.7), second in EPA per play, first in success rate, fourth in opponent EPA per play, and eighth in opponent success rate. They're well-balanced on both sides of the ball, and now they get to host a bad Commanders team in a prime time slot. There's a chance this game gets ugly. Brock Purdy has thrown at least two scores in every game this season, and he has two games with three or more touchdown passes (against the Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals). Washington has given up the most touchdown passes in the league (14) through five weeks, and Jameis Winston torched this secondary in the second half of Week 5. Overall, the Commanders are 23rd in EPA/Pass and 29th in passing yards allowed in 2026. This is a dream matchup for Purdy, who has thrown the ball just over 28 times per game for the offense that is No. 1 in success rate and No. 2 in EPA/Play this season. At +146, I think this prop is worth a shot against one of the worst pass defenses in the NFL. Jayden Daniels has only played in three games this season, but the Commanders quarterback has 203 rushing yards and two scores. Now, 103 of those yards came in Week 5 against the New York Giants, but Daniels has cleared this rushing yards total twice, picking up over 60 yards in two of his games. The 49ers’ defense is a top-five unit in EPA/Rush, so I expect plenty of dropbacks for Daniels on Monday night. Since the star quarterback has such a unique rushing ability, I wouldn’t be shocked if he escapes the pocket a few times for long scrambles. After all, Daniels has at least five carries in every game this season, including nine in his return from a dislocated elbow. If I’m betting on Purdy to throw three scores, I might as well take Mike Evans to catch one! away.blurb: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers Skip to main content SI.COM The Washington Commanders' final injury report lists a baker's dozen of players out or questionable, sure to create an availability problem for Washington facing the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Four players are officially listed as out: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee) , and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle). All four players missed practice all week. Nine additional players are also listed as questionable, including Stefon Diggs, Javon Kinlaw, and three safeties. Of the three safeties, Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice but were upgraded to limited; Nick Cross (illness) was a full participant all three days but is still questionable. All three players missed last week's game against New York . Quan Martin improved from limited on Thursday to full participation on Friday and Saturday, with no game designation. Stefon Diggs' return is possible; he's officially listed as questionable. He went from missing Thursday's practice to limited on both Friday and Saturday. Terry McLaurin has no game designation after being limited Thursday and Saturday and sitting out Friday with a hamstring/rest designation. Treylon Burks was also limited all three days but has no game designation. Getting Diggs back would give Jayden Daniels another option in the passing game after playing without him against the Giants. The Commanders will also be without Croskey-Merritt in the backfield , but they should have options. Austin Ekeler was limited all week with a chest injury, while Rachaad White went from full participation Thursday to limited Friday and Saturday. Neither received a game designation. Jeremy McNichols was a full participant all three days but remains questionable with a quad injury. He would also need to be activated from injured reserve before he can play Monday. Washington Commanders PR Washington's defensive front is another area to watch with Omenihu and Jean-Baptiste both out. Kinlaw fully participated Thursday, missed Friday's practice, and returned Saturday on a limited basis. He's questionable with ankle and knee injuries. K'Lavon Chaisson, meanwhile, returned to full participation Saturday after sitting out Friday and has no game designation. There are still a few roster decisions to make before Monday night. Trey Amos (ankle) and Jordan Magee (hamstring) are both questionable and, like McNichols, remain in their 21-day practice windows. Neither can play until they are activated from their respective reserve lists. Lucas Patrick is also questionable with an illness despite returning to full participation Saturday. Washington knows which four players it won't have against San Francisco, but with nine more listed as questionable, the Commanders still have plenty to sort out before Monday night's kickoff. Quinn also told reporters that quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), edge rusher Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pec) and defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) have been ruled out versus San Francisco and won't make the trip to the Bay Area. home.headline: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers
home.blurb: Commanders' Final Injury Report: Four Out, Nine Questionable vs. Unbeaten 49ers Skip to main content SI.COM The Washington Commanders' final injury report lists a baker's dozen of players out or questionable, sure to create an availability problem for Washington facing the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Four players are officially listed as out: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee) , and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle). All four players missed practice all week. Nine additional players are also listed as questionable, including Stefon Diggs, Javon Kinlaw, and three safeties. Of the three safeties, Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice but were upgraded to limited; Nick Cross (illness) was a full participant all three days but is still questionable. All three players missed last week's game against New York . Quan Martin improved from limited on Thursday to full participation on Friday and Saturday, with no game designation. Stefon Diggs' return is possible; he's officially listed as questionable. He went from missing Thursday's practice to limited on both Friday and Saturday. Terry McLaurin has no game designation after being limited Thursday and Saturday and sitting out Friday with a hamstring/rest designation. Treylon Burks was also limited all three days but has no game designation. Getting Diggs back would give Jayden Daniels another option in the passing game after playing without him against the Giants. The Commanders will also be without Croskey-Merritt in the backfield , but they should have options. Austin Ekeler was limited all week with a chest injury, while Rachaad White went from full participation Thursday to limited Friday and Saturday. Neither received a game designation. Jeremy McNichols was a full participant all three days but remains questionable with a quad injury. He would also need to be activated from injured reserve before he can play Monday. Washington Commanders PR Washington's defensive front is another area to watch with Omenihu and Jean-Baptiste both out. Kinlaw fully participated Thursday, missed Friday's practice, and returned Saturday on a limited basis. He's questionable with ankle and knee injuries. K'Lavon Chaisson, meanwhile, returned to full participation Saturday after sitting out Friday and has no game designation. There are still a few roster decisions to make before Monday night. Trey Amos (ankle) and Jordan Magee (hamstring) are both questionable and, like McNichols, remain in their 21-day practice windows. Neither can play until they are activated from their respective reserve lists. Lucas Patrick is also questionable with an illness despite returning to full participation Saturday. Washington knows which four players it won't have against San Francisco, but with nine more listed as questionable, the Commanders still have plenty to sort out before Monday night's kickoff.
